$comment: The source of sf-input-color's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js). Taken from simai/ui-control control/smart-architecture/migration/out/color (migration/convert-1.3.8.mjs from simai/ui-source@5100227 src/smart/color/smart.manifest.json); standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8, vocabulary 1.1.5. Its x-todo are decided in x-decisions.

size.summary: The size ladder step, so a colour beside a text field lines up with it.

appearance.summary: How the swatch in the field is bounded: bordered (the hairline of outline-variant), outlined (the field's stronger outline) or plain (no border). The paint stays inside the border, so the three looks differ (CO-06).

variant.summary: What the control is. field: a field of the control ladder -- the swatch, the value and a chevron -- that opens the Framework's own colour window. theme: only a circle of the current colour, as a site header holds it (C84); it opens the same window at its normal size, with no text and no theme row. brand: the field, for a settings screen («Оформление», C84), with what a person should know about the colour as lines under it (core themeChecks). theme and brand are the brand colour: they rebuild the theme from the colour while it moves (SF.ThemePalette: the four dynamic palettes, never a status, and the brand fill --sf-brand, --sf-on-brand of a header and a cover) on target, committing it when a colour is chosen. Their value is always a code and takes no alpha.

target.summary: variant theme or brand: a CSS selector of the element the theme is put on, as inline variables (a settings screen's preview, so the admin keeps its own colours); empty, the document's root. A selector that names nothing puts the theme nowhere.

swatches.summary: The colours a product already has, comma separated, each #hex, #hex|Name or a palette name (blue|Name); a name may hold spaces. A piece without a name may list several colours by spaces. They are the first row of the window's palette view, so a person picks the brand colour rather than matching a hex by eye.

palette.summary: Whether the window's palette view shows the sixteen hues of the static palette (C17). A hue is stored by its name (blue), the same in every language; the field shows the translated word and the theme picks the tone (50 light, 70 dark). palette="false": only the product's swatches, or «Своё» alone.

custom.summary: Whether the window offers «Своё», an own colour: the shade area, the eyedropper where the browser has one, the hue strip and the code row «format | code». custom="false" keeps the palette only (task labels, chart series). Without a palette «Своё» is always offered.

alpha.summary: Whether an own colour may be translucent: the alpha strip and the % field are drawn and the value may be #rrggbbaa. Without it a translucent code keeps its colour and drops the alpha, and translucent recent colours are not shown.

clearable.summary: Whether a chosen colour can be returned to the inherited one. With variant theme: a second button takes the theme back to what the page had before the control changed it (the Framework colour unless the page set its own).

name.summary: The form name. A hidden input carries the value under it, empty while the inherited colour applies.

label.summary: The field's label, drawn above the row as sf-input's label and naming the colour input (1.6.0). For a name without a visible label, write aria-label.

choose-label.summary: The words on the swatch. Unset, the component answers in the page's language ("Choose a colour" in English).

clear-label.summary: The words on the control that returns to the inherited colour. Unset, it follows the page's language; with variant theme the default is the theme words ("Use the original theme colour").

value.summary: The colour: a palette name (red, orange, amber, yellow, lime, green, teal, cyan, sky, blue, indigo, violet, purple, pink, brown, gray), stored the same in every language, or the code of an own colour, #rrggbb (or #rrggbbaa with alpha; #rgb and #rgba are read and stored long, lowercase). Empty means nothing is chosen and the inherited colour applies. variants theme and brand store a code.

effective-value.summary: What is painted: the value when there is one, the inherited colour when there is not (§4.3); it was the getter `shown`, which the base value shown (§4.1) now names

theme.summary: variants theme and brand: the theme the colour makes now (simai.framework.theme), or null before SF.ThemePalette has loaded; a field without a value makes the inherited or the Framework's own colour's theme

checks.summary: variants theme and brand: what a person should know about the colour (core themeChecks): [{code, level, ...}] -- contrast, adjusted, close-to-status, grey; empty when there is nothing to say. The brand field draws them as lines under itself.

change.summary: A colour was committed: once when a swatch is chosen, a drag across the shade area or a strip is released, the code field is left or Enter pressed, a key on a strip rests, or clear is pressed -- not on every step of a drag. Carries the value and the form name; an empty value means the inherited colour applies again. With variant theme or brand and a value, it also carries the theme, its variables (the four palettes and the brand fill), its CSS as a :root rule and its checks -- the names sf-theme-generator's events carried.

input.summary: The colour moved: on every step of a drag across the shade area or a strip, on each key in the code field that reads as a colour, and before each change. Carries the value and the form name. With variant theme or brand, the theme, variables, css and checks as change carries them.

field-reset.summary: The person pressed the reset back to the inherited value. The event of the trait field-inherit@1: one name for every field of the family, so a form hears them all at once and tells them apart by detail.tag. Fired before the field is emptied and cancellable: preventDefault keeps the value. When it is not prevented the field empties, says so with its ordinary change, shows the inherited value again and takes focus back.

tag.summary: The element that was reset, as a tag name.

value.summary: The field's own value before the reset.

inherited-value.summary: The inherited value it returns to.

name.summary: The form name, empty when the field has none.

clear.summary: Return to the inherited colour; the same as setValue(""). Returns whether it changed.

relations.name: cl-segmented
$comment: cl-segmented: the window's «Палитра / Своё» switch, drawn only once the window opens, fetched after the page is ready.

aliases.$comment: Dated aliases for the shim (core/js/aliases.js, standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8 §16.20). Event rows send the new name first, then the old one, with one detail; setting rows map the old attribute and property to the new; host-attribute rows (no "to") stay host attributes read by the browser or the base and are listed, refused by the shim on purpose; documentary rows ("shim": "none") record a rename the shim cannot serve.

rows.note: the event of the trait field-inherit@1, declared in component.json as the shared event field-reset; the field sends sf-field-reset and the shim follows it with this dated name, same detail, one cancel
rows.summary: The person pressed the reset back to the inherited value. Fired before the field is emptied and cancellable: preventDefault keeps the value. When it is not prevented the field empties, says so with its ordinary change, shows the inherited value again and takes focus back.

rows.note: the getter shown returned the painted colour; shown is now the base value (a boolean) on every element, so the old meaning cannot be served beside it: read effectiveValue

rows.section: rename plan R0 (ui-control RENAME-PLAN-2026-11-03), naming decision 2026-11-02
rows.note: the element is sf-input-color; sf-color is a subclass defined beside it until the date

x-summary: A colour field: a swatch, the value and a chevron that open the Framework's own compact window -- the static palette first, the product's own colours, recent own colours and «Своё» (shade area, eyedropper, hue and alpha strips, a code in Hex, RGB, HSL or HSB) -- and a way back to an inherited colour. The value is a palette name or a code. Built as a general part because a colour is set in a theme, in a site look, on a label and on a chart series, not only on a record.
x-renamed: the getter shown -> the value effective-value: shown is the base value of every element (§4.1), a boolean; the colour it returned is effective-value (§4.3), a dated documentary row in aliases.json
x-decisions: trait-words: the field-inherit@1 words (inherited, reset, described) live in this component's lang runtime until a trait folder holds them (Annex A item 13); the shared INHERITED_TEXT stays the class components' fallback
key-effects: Enter and Space on a swatch select its colour; on the platform picker input they open it (the browser's own)
template: the default template stays the Lit module js/templates/default.js, the migration form §5.2 allows; template.html follows when the build compiles HTML templates
examples: examples.json written from the docs (the folder had no Studio fixture)

css-variables: five public variables read by js/templates/default.css with the role token as fallback (§6); a state the public-variables probe cannot draw at rest (hover, an outline) takes no variable of its own yet
version: 1.2.0 -- the value effective-value is added and the getter shown leaves for the base value behind a dated row; a minor (§4.10)
shown: renamed effective-value; the shim cannot serve the old name, because shown is the base value (§4.1) on every element, so the row is documentary (shim none)

actions.clear answers an outcome (§4.4): applied, or refused with reason unchanged when there was nothing to clear; setValue stays a method of the class outside the interface (a person-like write that sends input and change)

form: the host is the form control through ElementInternals (§17.1); it submits the chosen hex, empty while the inherited colour applies (§20.2); the hidden input is drawn only without ElementInternals
version 1.2.1: the first-paint sheet list names the utility sheets its templates draw with (core.runtime 1.0.7 asks for them before the element draws: the style gate).

version 1.2.3: the bundle carries no element layer of its own -- element-manifest, aliases, the alias table, the host port, deprecations, page actions, the layer stack, the open-surface mark and the instance path come from the page's shared runtime (SF.runtimeModule, runtime ABI 1, core.runtime 1.1.0), one instance per page -- and embeds of this file only the keys the runtime reads. Behaviour unchanged.

version 1.3.0: variant theme (owner decision by delegation, 2026-10-28: a theme colour button is a variant of sf-color, not a separate component). An icon-only primary sf-icon-button (icon palette) opens the native colour input by showPicker (a click on it where showPicker is missing); the input stays in the tree, transparent and out of the focus order, so the picker anchors at the button. input moves the value and applies the theme to <html> after 120 ms of quiet; change commits, applies at once and sends change once. A moved colour that is never committed (Escape, cancel) goes back to the committed one when the browser restores the input, or at the next press or key on the page. Empty value = the theme the page had: the control restores the variables applyTheme changed. SF.ThemePalette comes through the Loader (ensurePlugin theme-palette, the theme-palette:ready event), not inside this bundle: the HCT solver and tonal palettes are about 70 KB of source, more than the colour control itself, and every field-variant colour would carry them. No storage: the page keeps the value; a value written from code applies the theme silently.

version 1.4.0: the trait event is declared in component.json as the shared event field-reset (standard 1.3.13 §8: an event a trait brings is named sf-<verb>, with no tag): the element sends sf-field-reset itself and the manifest describes it, with tag in the detail. Before, the registry described only the retired sf-field:reset and no current name, and the new name came from the alias shim alone. The dated sf-field:reset follows with the same detail and one cancel until 2026-12-01.

version 1.5.0: the tag is sf-input-color (naming decision 2026-11-02: sf-[set]-<block>[-<variant>]); the folder, the id smart.input-color and the bundle cl-input-color follow it. sf-color stays a dated alias until 2027-01-01: a subclass the Smart base defines beside the new tag, listed in the rule, in sheets as :is(sf-input-color, sf-color) (change journal tag-sf-color-to-sf-input-color, path-smart-color-to-input-color).

version 1.5.1: the inherited state comes with the family's hidden note (helpers/inherited-value.js, syncInheritedNote): when something else describes the control through aria-describedby, the inherited sentence is named there too, because a browser reads aria-describedby instead of aria-description. Nothing else describes the colour input, so it reads the same.

version 1.5.2: the sf-button and sf-button-icon it draws are asked for their current names (appearance ghost for link, status danger for error; actions block, decisions C13 and C15), so the template uses no dated alias; nothing it draws changes.

version 1.5.5 (2026-11-09): a patch; nothing in the component changed. A shared sheet it draws with moved in the next block (src/smart/helpers/inherited-value.css, the C27 inherited-value reset), so the component takes a patch with it.

version 1.5.4: the size rule C18 (2026-11-09): the presets' gap reads --sf-space-1/2 with no raw fallback (the fallback said 4px, the token is 8/12 and always defined; nothing moves). Also: the row wraps (flex-wrap: wrap): the chip, the value, the swatches and the inherited slot no longer stand past a narrow container -- inside sf-theme-generator the row was 314px wide in a 288px column at 320px and the reported 17px at a 390px screen; a row that fits is drawn as before.

version 1.6.0 (2026-11-11): one field label look for every field (dispatcher decision a, docs pre-check 2026-11-10 FB-10, CO-04): `label` is drawn above the row as sf-input's label (14 regular on-surface-variant at size 1) and still names the colour input; a colour with a name and no visible label takes the host's aria-label (the field renderers and the site header's tools now pass aria-label). The product colours are controls of the row's size, as tall as the chip and the reset (C01, CO-03; they were one rung down). The theme variant is unchanged.

version 1.6.1 (2026-11-11): a patch, nothing drawn differently. The sheet reads the C16 roles by their current names where it read the former ones, which are var() of them wherever they are declared (src/core/contracts/token-aliases.v1.json, sf-role-aliases): --sf-on-disable → --sf-on-surface-disabled. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.7.0 (2026-11-12, owner decisions C83 and C86, round 4 R167-R170, C84; defects CO-03, CO-06, CO-07): a minor. The field is a field of the control ladder -- a swatch (the text's square on the C77 inset), the value and a chevron in one frame of the size's control height -- that opens the Framework's own compact window, never the browser's colour dialog (R130). The window is 304 wide (eight 1/3-rung swatches, 8 apart, 12 inside), anchored under the field by core's positioning (flip, shift, never taller than its room) in the top layer, and a sheet at the bottom of the screen below 44rem. «Палитра / Своё» is the standard sf-segmented; «Палитра» holds the product's swatches, the sixteen static hues (C17) and, after a divider, the recent own colours; «Своё» holds the shade area, the eyedropper (only where window.EyeDropper exists; disabled with its reason elsewhere), the hue strip, the alpha strip and one joined row «format | code | %» (Hex, RGB, HSL, HSB; any CSS colour may be pasted). New settings palette (default true), custom (default true) and alpha (default false). The value is a palette name (one in every language, painted 50 light / 70 dark) or a code; #rrggbbaa only with alpha. Recent own colours: one list per site, a view preference (SF.Preferences key sf-color-recent), 16 kept, 8 shown, own colours only, translucent ones hidden in a field without alpha (R168). Every swatch has one painter: the paint is clipped inside its 1 px border (R169) and a translucent colour is drawn split -- the left half without alpha, the right half as it is over the checkerboard (C86). CO-03: one height in the row (the product colours moved into the window). CO-06: bordered, outlined and plain now differ (the paint no longer runs under the border; plain has none). CO-07: the inherited colour shows in the value's place, the marker at the frame's end. variant theme (C84): only a circle of the current colour that opens the same window at its normal size; its value is always a code (a palette hue is stored as its tone's code); the native colour input and the uncommitted-colour watch are gone (the window commits each choice). New methods openPicker({anchor, view}) and closePicker(). Words: the hue names, the window's labels.

version 1.7.0, also (2026-11-12, owner decision C84: the brand colour is a mode of this field, sf-theme-generator leaves with a dated alias): variant brand -- the field of a settings screen, with the colour's checks (core themeChecks: contrast, adjusted, close-to-status, grey) as lines in a polite status region under it, the words sf-theme-generator had. Variants theme and brand put the theme -- the four dynamic palettes, never a status (TG-01; info stays sky under every brand, C90) -- and the brand fill of a header and a cover (--sf-brand, --sf-on-brand, core brandVariables: a light colour as it is with black or white text, any other the primary role) on target (new setting: a selector, empty the document's root); change and input of these variants carry theme, variables, css and checks, as the generator's events did. Values theme and checks. Neither takes alpha.

version 1.7.1 (2026-11-13, C83 acceptance; one number above the unreleased 1.7.0 it joins): a patch. The field holds its control's height from the first paint: .sf-color-field > .sf-color takes the size's control height as its least height, so a printed snapshot or a host that has not upgraded yet no longer draws a shorter row (40 px against the field's 56) and the page does not move when the element takes over. The upgraded field is the same to the pixel. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

$comment: The colour control loads on demand like any other Smart element. Its relations are
the icons, the icon button of the reset and the eyedropper, and the segmented
switch of its own window (lazy: drawn only once the window opens).

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-input-color wherever a colour is set -- a theme, a site look, a label, a chart series -- and especially when the colour may be left unset to inherit one. For labels and chart series keep the palette name (custom="false"), so the colour follows the dark theme.
do_not: Do not draw the inherited colour as the value: pass it as inherited-value so «not set» stays distinguishable
Do not listen to input for saving; save on change, which fires once per committed colour
Do not turn a palette name into a hex before storing it: the name follows the theme, the hex does not
Do not copy generated ui-smart code
Do not move host data or access decisions into the component
ai_guidance.minimal_example: <sf-input-color label="Brand colour" clearable inherited-value="blue" swatches="#1f6feb|Brand blue, red|Alert"></sf-input-color>

accessibility.focus: The field's trigger takes focus and keeps a visible focus ring on the frame; it names the field and the colour («Цвет метки: Синий») and says aria-haspopup dialog and aria-expanded. The window is a labelled dialog: focus goes to the chosen swatch (or the shade area in «Своё»), each swatch group is a radio group with one tab stop and arrow keys, the shade area and the strips are sliders with aria-valuetext, Escape closes the window and focus returns to the trigger. After a reset back to the inherited value, focus returns to the trigger; while the value is inherited, the trigger carries it as aria-description and the visible marker is aria-hidden.

sf-field:reset.summary: The person pressed the reset back to the inherited value. Fired before the field is emptied and cancellable: preventDefault keeps the value. When it is not prevented the field empties, says so with its ordinary change, shows the inherited value again and takes focus back.

value.description: The field's own value before the reset.

inheritedValue.description: The inherited value it returns to.

name.description: The form name, empty when the field has none.

setValue.summary: Set and commit the colour as a person would: normalised, reflected to value, input and then change dispatched when it differs from the committed one. Returns whether the value changed.

resetToInherited.summary: Returns the field to its inherited value, as the reset button does: fires the cancellable sf-field-reset, then empties the own value and focuses the control. Returns whether it was reset (false without an inherited value, without an own value, while disabled or readonly, or when the event was prevented).

openPicker.summary: Opens the colour window on the view the value comes from, or on {view: 'palette' | 'own'}. {anchor} places it against an element of the page and gives focus back to it on close (a settings menu row, C85), instead of the field. Returns whether it is open (false while disabled).

closePicker.summary: Closes the colour window and returns focus to the trigger unless {restoreFocus: false}. Returns true.

inherited-value.description: The colour that applies while nothing is chosen. Shown as inherited rather than drawn as the value: a control that drew it as the value would make «not set» and «set to the same colour» look identical, and only one of them follows the theme when the theme changes.

inherited-text.description: What is read in place of a value while nothing is chosen. Unset, it follows the page's language.

reset-label.description: The accessible name of the button that returns to the inherited colour; `clear-label` still names it. Unset, it follows the page's language («Reset to inherited», «Сбросить к наследуемому»).
